ratings_why.fun: Every shop is a menu of texts, and the unlisted chains are the joy: Tam Twice wearing your own Bettie Underhill or Grandfer Acorn doubles a payoff, and Tod plus Wicker Moll turns one shop unit into three wears; that hidden overlap earns it over a 7.
ratings_why.distinct: No current tribe borrows other tribes' text and tribe tags; a Changeling that is an Ooze and a Bog unit at once, taking Harvest Supper bonuses, plays unlike anything in Battlegrounds or a generic auto-battler, which earns the 8.

verdict_why: One real readability fix: how a plain Stock wears its remembered unit, which decides whether the Alder Whittler does anything.

points.text: Stock says it 'can wear that unit, at most once' but not how or when; if any bought Stock can wear on its own, the Alder Whittler is nearly blank. Say a Stock wears only when a card makes it (Whittler, Wicker Moll), or give it Guise limited to its remembered unit.

Tam Twice wearing your own Wicker Moll, Bettie Underhill or Lady Under the Hill is the tribe's best hidden combo; say whether two Molls give a Stock +3/+3 twice and whether two Ladies stack, so the combo is readable rather than argued over.

Tod's sale-wear is not once a turn, so buy Stock, sell Stock, Tod wears it gives a 1-gold wear for Bettie, Nursemaid and Pedlar; that's a great Johnny line, keep it and just test the gold-to-stats rate.
Coat-Peg Steward gathers guises mid-fight, after Start of Combat; a line on whether gathered 'When this dies' or attack texts work at once would make it a planned piece rather than a surprise.
Grandfer Acorn worn by Tam gives Tam the 3-guise text too, so a second stack grows over turns; worth naming in build C as the deep line.

standouts.why: Wearing your own board turns every payoff, even Changeling payoffs, into something you can double; the deepest card in the tribe.
Selling becomes a wear, so goldens you outgrow, Stocks and tempo bodies all feed the engine; real decisions every turn.
Reading the next opponent's board to place a Changeling across their best text is a positioning puzzle few tribes offer.

weakest.why: Pure Guise on a vanilla body; fine as the seed, but nothing to combo with beyond what it wears.
Bee Orchid is a flat End of Turn buffer for wearers, the one obvious job the Nursemaid already covers.
Porter is a pure number lift; useful, but no interaction beyond reaching higher texts.

flags.note: With Moll and Tod, one Stock can be three wears for 1 gold; Bettie on 6-7 Changelings can then go well past the Tier 6 top. Bounded by gold, not looped.
Wiping four enemy texts at Start of Combat is a hard counter to text carries; the opponent can only answer by positioning.
When and how a plain bought Stock wears its remembered unit isn't stated.
Doubled copies of Moll or the Lady via Tam: whether their effects stack isn't stated.
